questions.statute_citation: Texas DPS Driver Examination Manual — Dimension II (Positioning)
questions.visual_description: Top-down view of 3 vehicles approaching a solid white stop line. Vehicle 1 centered in lane, Vehicle 2 hugging centerline, Vehicle 3 drifting to shoulder.
questions.prompt: During the Texas DPS driving examination, an applicant's vehicle positioning is strictly evaluated. Which vehicle demonstrates the legally correct lane positioning prior to the stop line?

options.text: Vehicle 1, centered evenly within lane boundaries with full forward visibility
Vehicle 2, straddling the centerline to anticipate an immediate left turn
Vehicle 3, riding the outer shoulder to yield roadway center to others
Vehicle 2, crowding oncoming traffic to discourage vehicles from passing

questions.statutory_rationale: Under Texas DPS Road Test grading criteria, 'Positioning' requires maintaining the vehicle squarely centered within the marked travel lane, without crowding oncoming traffic or drifting onto roadway shoulders.

questions.statute_citation: TDLR ADE Standards §4.1.1.1(B) & Texas DPS Road Test Scoring Rubric
questions.prompt: The Texas DPS road test specifically grades candidates across four fundamental driving competencies. Which group accurately lists these four core evaluation categories?

options.text: Acceleration, Braking, Steering, and Parking
Control, Observation, Positioning, and Signaling
Speed, Navigation, Right-of-Way, and Courtesy
Inspection, Maintenance, Reaction, and Shifting

questions.statutory_rationale: Texas DPS examiners grade applicants on four designated basic skills (abbreviated COPS): Control (steering & vehicle handling), Observation (scanning traffic), Positioning (lane placement), and Signaling (communicating intent).

questions.visual_description: Overhead corridor view with lead car passing a green highway landmark, trailing car behind it, annotated with 3-Second Time Buffer.
questions.prompt: Under Texas defensive driving standards, how should a driver use a fixed roadside marker to verify a safe following distance under good weather conditions?

options.text: Match the speedometer reading directly to the distance between markers
Maintain one vehicle length for every fifteen miles per hour traveled
Count at least three seconds after the vehicle ahead passes the marker
Accelerate until the lead vehicle aligns with the next road landmark

questions.statutory_rationale: The Texas Driver Handbook establishes the 'three-second rule' for safe following distance under good weather. When the lead car passes a fixed landmark, count 'one-thousand-one, one-thousand-two, one-thousand-three'. Reaching it sooner indicates following too closely.

questions.prompt: When encountering adverse driving conditions such as heavy rain or fog, how does Texas law require a driver to adapt their operating speed?

options.text: Maintain the posted speed limit to prevent sudden rear-end collisions
Drive five miles per hour under the limit with hazard lights flashing
Match the speed of surrounding traffic regardless of reduced traction
Reduce speed below the posted limit to what is reasonable and prudent

questions.statutory_rationale: Texas Transportation Code §545.351 mandates that an operator may not drive at a speed greater than is reasonable and prudent under prevailing road and weather conditions, regardless of maximum posted limits.

questions.visual_description: Technical cross-section diagram comparing legal tire tread channeling water (≥ 2/32") vs bald tire hydroplaning (< 2/32").
questions.prompt: According to Texas vehicle inspection laws, what is the minimum legal tire tread depth required across the roadway contact surface?

options.text: At least 4/32 of an inch across the center tread contact
At least 2/32 of an inch of tread in all major grooves
At least 1/16 of an inch measured only on the outer ribs
At least 3/32 of an inch exclusively on front axle tires

questions.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §548.051 and Texas Department of Public Safety inspection regulations, passenger vehicle tires must have a minimum tread depth of at least 2/32 (or 1/16) inch in all major grooves to pass annual safety inspection.
